posts.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
posts.label: 📜✍️ Signed by Pres. Trump
posts.summary: The law funds federal agencies through December 11, 2026, at current spending levels while preventing a government shutdown, with exceptions that provide additional or flexible funding for programs like nutrition assistance, disaster relief, and wildfire suppression. It also extends expiring authorities for agriculture, flood insurance, cybersecurity, transportation, veterans benefits, housing, and trade programs, while temporarily blocking certain regulatory changes and freezing congressional pay adjustments.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO)
posts.whatsNext: Takes effect (on enactment unless the text sets other dates)

posts.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices.
posts.label: ❌ Failed passage (212-206)
posts.summary: The joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would require the Supreme Court to consist of exactly nine justices—one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.
posts.whatsNext: No further action scheduled (it can be brought back)

posts.title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would extend through the end of 2028 duty-free trade benefits that allow most exports from eligible sub-Saharan African countries to enter the U.S. market without tariffs, while also extending customs user fees through the end of 2031. It would also allow for refunds of duties paid on African imports that entered the country after September 30, 2025.
posts.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. Jason Smith (R-MO)
posts.whatsNext: President has 10 days (Sundays excepted): sign, veto, or it becomes law unsigned (pocket veto if adjournment prevents return)

posts.title: Hershel ‘Woody' Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act
posts.label: 📌 Presented to President
posts.summary: The bill would authorize the National Medal of Honor Museum Foundation to build a commemorative monument on the National Mall honoring Medal of Honor recipients for their acts of valor and sacrifice. The monument would be required to be located within the central area of the National Mall, between the Capitol and Lincoln Memorial.
